changes: Converted from the official PDF to Markdown by the your5e/5e-srd-markdown project, which lists its own changes: it gave class tables with several header rows a single header row; added a “Traits” heading to stat blocks; fixed the “Components” typo in Contagion; set “Petrifying Gaze” in bold italics like other traits; split the Armor, Saddles, Scrying, Tack, Harness, and Drawn Vehicles and Weapons tables at their mid-table headings; moved each pantheon’s table of deities into its description; added subclass introduction headings to the Barbarian, Bard, Cleric and Druid; and laid out the monster ability tables as score, modifier and saving throw in place of the Saving Throws line. mistLAB converted that Markdown to HTML and JSON, reformatted and indexed it, and, checked against the official PDF, restored what the Markdown had dropped: seven spell-list entries (Heroes’ Feast for the Cleric and Druid, Hunter’s Mark for the Ranger, Enlarge/Reduce for the Sorcerer and Wizard, Arcanist’s Magic Aura and Control Weather for the Wizard), the Grimlock’s Blind Senses trait, the Jokers row of the Deck of Illusions table, the Cleric Level column of the Destroy Undead table and the Saving Throws line of each stat block. It also made “Meat, chunk” its own row of the Food, Drink, and Lodging table as printed, set the Warlock table’s “Bonus Proficiency” heading back to “Proficiency Bonus” and the Confusion table’s “Behaviour” back to “Behavior” as printed, rejoined “Tent, two-person”, put back the hyphens the Markdown had dropped where the PDF breaks a line (all-night, briar-choked, fast-talk, fog-shrouded, foot-by, foot-cube, foot-radius, foot-wide, good-aligned, half-dragon, hand-to, higher-level, higher-than, life-threatening, long-dead, mud-filled, self-expression, single-use, three-quarters, two-handed, white-hot) and the 13 dashes it had dropped there, and removed stray italics around punctuation. Apart from formatting and these changes, no rules text was changed.

Traits

Death Throes. When the balor dies, it explodes, and each creature within 30 feet of it must make a DC 20 Dexterity saving throw, taking 70 (20d6) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The explosion ignites flammable objects in that area that aren't being worn or carried, and it destroys the balor's weapons.

Fire Aura. At the start of each of the balor's turns, each creature within 5 feet of it takes 10 (3d6) fire damage, and flammable objects in the aura that aren't being worn or carried ignite. A creature that touches the balor or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it takes 10 (3d6) fire damage.

Magic Resistance. The balor has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

Magic Weapons. The balor's weapon attacks are magical.

Actions

Multiattack. The balor makes two attacks: one with its longsword and one with its whip.

Longsword. Melee Weapon Attack: +14 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 21 (3d8 + 8) slashing damage plus 13 (3d8) lightning damage. If the balor scores a critical hit, it rolls damage dice three times, instead of twice.

Whip. Melee Weapon Attack: +14 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (2d6 + 8) slashing damage plus 10 (3d6) fire damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 20 Strength saving throw or be pulled up to 25 feet toward the balor.

Teleport. The balor magically teleports, along with any equipment it is wearing or carrying, up to 120 feet to an unoccupied space it can see.
